mainTopic: ספק בכור in twins, and the גמרא's explanations of רבי מאיר's ruling when the father dies: רבי ירמיה's joint-ownership rule and רבא's five-סלעים case
overview: The משנה deals with twins born to a woman who never gave birth before, when no one knows which baby came out first. If both are boys, one is surely the בכור, so the father gives the כהן five סלעים. If one twin dies within thirty days, the father is exempt. If the twins are a boy and a girl, the כהן gets nothing. If the father dies, רבי מאיר says payment depends on whether the sons divided the estate, and רבי יהודה says the property is already obligated. The גמרא asks when the father died in רבי מאיר's case. It first tries 'within thirty days,' with each son pushing the כהן to his brother. רבי ירמיה learns from this that a creditor can collect from a field jointly owned by two men named יוסף בן שמעון. רבא rejects this approach, because property is only a guarantor and cannot owe more than its owner. Instead he says the father died after thirty days and left only five סלעים. He begins explaining this with רב אסי's rule that divided brothers are half heirs and half buyers, together with a rule about a מלוה הכתובה בתורה, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Twin boys: the father pays five סלעים
steps.stepSummary: If a woman's first birth is twin boys, the father must give the כהן five סלעים for פדיון הבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man whose wife never gave birth before, and then she had two boys, gives five סלעים to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with twin boys born to a woman who never gave birth before. The father must pay the כהן five סלעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We don't know which twin came out first, but one of them is definitely the בכור. So the father owes one פדיון payment of five סלעים, not ten. It doesn't matter which twin is the בכור, because either way the payment is owed.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the core teaching being studied)
She had her first birth (opening the womb for the first time)
Five סלעים, the payment for פדיון הבן
The priest who receives the redemption money

phrases.english: MISHNAH
One whose wife had not previously given birth
and she gave birth to two males (twins)
phrases.notes: No one knows which came out first.

phrases.english: he gives five sela coins to the priest.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: With twin boys, one of them is surely the בכור, so the father pays five סלעים.

steps.title: If one twin dies within thirty days, the father is exempt
steps.stepSummary: If one of the twins dies before thirty days, the father pays nothing, because maybe the one who died was the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died within thirty days, the father is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a case: one twin dies before the thirty-day point. The father no longer has to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obligation of פדיון only starts after thirty days. If a twin dies before then, it is possible he was the בכור, and a בכור who dies before thirty days needs no פדיון. Because of this doubt, the כהן cannot demand payment.

keyTerms.meaning: Within thirty days, before the פדיון obligation begins

phrases.english: If one of them died
within thirty days,
the father is exempt.
phrases.notes: Maybe the one who died was the בכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case where the obligation from step 1 does not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubt about whether the dead twin was the בכור exempts the father.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: if the father dies, it depends on whether the sons divided the estate
steps.stepSummary: When the father dies and both sons are alive, רבי מאיר says a payment made before they divided the estate stays with the כהן. If they did not pay before dividing, they are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the father died and the sons are alive, רבי מאיר says: if they gave before they divided the property, what they gave is given. If not, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case: the father dies while both twins are alive. רבי מאיר makes the outcome depend on the sons dividing the inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the division, money paid to the כהן from the shared estate stays paid. Once the sons have split the property, they are exempt. The גמרא will soon ask why dividing makes such a difference.

keyTerms.meaning: They divided the inheritance between themselves

phrases.english: If the father died and the sons are alive,
Rabbi Meir says:
if they gave before they divided the property,
they have given it (it stays with the priest),
and if not, they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת הָאָב וְהַבָּנִים קַיָּימִים, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a payment made before division stands, but after division the sons are exempt.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the obligation already rests on the property
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the father's property is already obligated, so the sons must pay in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the property has already become obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר. He holds that the debt to the כהן is attached to the estate, so the heirs must pay whether or not they divided it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the obligation is not just personal. It sits on the property itself, like a lien. Dividing the estate therefore changes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The property has become obligated (a debt rests on it)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The property has already become obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The debt rests on the estate, so the heirs must always pay.

steps.title: A boy and a girl: the כהן gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: If the twins are a boy and a girl and we don't know who came out first, the כהן receives nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A male and a female: the כהן has nothing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with boy-girl twins. Nothing is paid to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the girl was born first. If so, the boy did not open the womb and is not a בכור. Because of this doubt, the כהן cannot collect.
steps.whatToRemember: With twin boys, one is surely a בכור, so payment is owed. With a boy and a girl, the boy may not be a בכור, so nothing is owed.

phrases.english: A male and a female (twins),
the priest has nothing here.
phrases.notes: Maybe the girl came out first.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Boy-girl twins create a doubt, so the כהן collects nothing.

steps.title: When did the father die?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the father died in רבי מאיר's case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking about the timing of the father's death in רבי מאיר's case. This sets up the next steps, which test each possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timing matters because the פדיון obligation starts at thirty days. If the father was alive at thirty days, the debt fell on him and his property. If he died earlier, it never fell on him.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA
The father died, when?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case behind רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did the father die after thirty days or within thirty days?

steps.title: It cannot mean the father died after thirty days
steps.stepSummary: If the father died after thirty days, his property already carries a lien, so how could רבי מאיר exempt the sons after dividing?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he died after thirty days, would רבי מאיר say in this case that once they divided they are exempt? But the property is already on lien!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and rejects it. If the father lived past thirty days, the debt is already attached to his property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A debt that took effect during the father's life creates a שעבוד on his property. Dividing the estate cannot remove a lien. So רבי מאיר could not possibly exempt the sons in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces an option that will be rejected)
They became subject to a lien

phrases.english: If you say that he died
after thirty days,
would Rabbi Meir say in this case
that when they divided, they are exempt?
But the property is already on lien!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, (לנכסי); the corrected wording is the one in square brackets, [נכסי].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבי מאיר's case as the father dying after thirty days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lien already rests on the property, and dividing the estate cannot cancel a lien.

steps.title: The father died within thirty days, so each son can push the כהן away
steps.stepSummary: The case must be that the father died within thirty days. After the sons divide the property, each son can send the כהן to his brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he died within thirty days. What is different when they divided? The כהן goes to this one and he pushes him away, then goes to that one and he pushes him away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers the second option: the father died before thirty days. It explains רבי מאיר's exemption after division by saying each son can refuse the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the father died before the debt began, it never fell on his property. Each son is only a ספק בכור. After division, each son can say, 'Prove I'm the בכור,' so the כהן cannot collect from either one.
steps.confusionAlert: 'מדחי ליה' does not mean the son denies the debt exists. It means each son says, 'Maybe it's my brother. Prove it's me.'

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he died within thirty days.
What is different when they divided?
That the priest goes to this son and he pushes him off,
and he goes to that son and he pushes him off;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected option from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (death within thirty days)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father died after thirty days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father died within thirty days, so after division each son can push the כהן to his brother.

steps.title: Each son could push the כהן away even before division
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation: the same refusal should work even before the sons divide the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even when they did not divide, let him go to this one and be pushed away, and go to that one and be pushed away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from step 8. If each son can refuse the כהן, he can do it before division too, so why does רבי מאיר imply that before division they must pay?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 relied on each son being able to say, 'Maybe it's my brother.' That argument does not depend on whether the property was divided. So the explanation does not account for the difference רבי מאיר makes between before and after division.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him push him away

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא must still find what makes division matter for רבי מאיר, and this drives the next part of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: Even when they did not divide, too,
let him go to this son and he will push him off,
and let him go to that son and he will push him off!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that after division each son can push the כהן away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pushing the כהן away has nothing to do with division, so it should also exempt the sons before division, yet רבי מאיר treats that case differently.

steps.title: A creditor can collect from a field owned by two men with the same name
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה infers a rule from our case. If two men named יוסף בן שמעון jointly own a field, a creditor of one of them can collect from it even without knowing which one owes him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: This teaches us something. Two men both named יוסף בן שמעון lived in the same city and bought a field together. A creditor of one of them can collect from that field. He can say to each one: 'If you are the one who owes me, I am taking your share. If your partner owes me, I am taking his share.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה learns a new rule from our case. Before the brothers divided, the כהן could collect from the shared estate even though neither brother alone could be forced to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each partner alone can say 'maybe it's not me.' But the creditor is not claiming from either person. He is taking from the joint field, and one share in it surely belongs to his debtor. This explains why the כהן collects before the division (answering step 9's challenge) but not after it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This teaches us' – introduces a rule inferred from an earlier case
A share or portion (here, a share in the field)

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a known rule about joint ownership: doubt about which partner is the debtor does not stop a creditor from collecting from property they own together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: This teaches us,
two people named Yosef ben Shimon
who lived in one city,
and they bought a field in partnership –
a creditor can collect it from them,
phrases.notes: He does not know which of the two is his debtor.

phrases.english: because he can say to him: If I have a claim against you –
I am taking your share,
and if I have a claim against your partner –
I am taking your partner's share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the 'died within thirty days' explanation. It also shows why the כהן can collect before division, which answers step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A creditor may collect from jointly owned property even when it is unclear which partner is his debtor, because one share surely belongs to the debtor.

steps.title: Property cannot be liable when the owner himself is not
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that a person's property is only a guarantor for him. A lender cannot collect from a guarantor when he cannot claim from the borrower himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person's property acts as a guarantor for him. Is there any case where you cannot claim from the person himself, yet you can claim from his guarantor?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the explanation from steps 8–10. That explanation said the כהן cannot claim from either brother personally, yet can take from their shared property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Property is only a backup for the person's own obligation, like a ערב (guarantor). If each brother can push the כהן away personally, his property should not be liable either. So the case of 'died within thirty days, collect from the joint estate' falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now consider' – opens a basic logical point

keyTerms.term: נִכְסֵי דְּבַר אִינִישׁ אִינּוּן עָרְבִין בֵּיהּ
keyTerms.meaning: A person's property acts as his guarantor

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about the two-יוסף בן שמעון case for its own sake. He is attacking the whole approach that has the כהן take from property he could not claim from either brother.

phrases.english: Rava said: Now consider,

phrases.aramaic: נִכְסֵי דְּבַר אִינִישׁ אִינּוּן עָרְבִין בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: a person's property is a guarantor for him,
is there anything
where he cannot claim from the debtor himself,
yet he can claim from the guarantor?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִכְּדֵי נִכְסֵי דְּבַר אִינִישׁ אִינּוּן עָרְבִין בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation that רבי ירמיה built on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the כהן collects from the shared estate even though he cannot claim from either brother personally.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Property is only a guarantor for its owner. A guarantor cannot be liable when the main debtor cannot be claimed from.

steps.title: A משנה shows you cannot go to the guarantor first
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports his objection with a משנה. A lender may not collect from the guarantor first, before claiming from the borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned in a משנה: One who lends to his friend with a guarantor may not collect from the guarantor. And we hold that this means he may not claim from the guarantor first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his objection from step 11 with a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (בבא בתרא קעג.) shows that a guarantor is only a second step after the borrower. The same is true of property. So it makes no sense for the כהן to collect from the brothers' property when he could not claim from the brothers themselves.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ עַל יְדֵי עָרֵב —
phrases.english: But we learned: One who lends to another with a guarantor –
may not collect from the guarantor,
and we hold
that he may not claim from the guarantor first!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ עַל יְדֵי עָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that supports רבא's objection.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that you cannot collect from a backup (guarantor or property) without a valid claim against the main debtor.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בבא בתרא about a loan with a guarantor.

steps.title: New explanation: the father died after thirty days, leaving only five סלעים
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the earlier explanation. The father died after thirty days. If the estate were large, the כהן would collect. The case is one where the whole estate was only five סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Really, the father died after thirty days. And if there were a lot of property, it is true that the כהן would take the money. But what case are we dealing with here? Where the whole estate is only five סלעים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a brand-new explanation of רבי מאיר's ruling. It replaces the 'died within thirty days' approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 asked how the lien could vanish if the father died after thirty days. רבא now accepts that case. He says the lien does work when there is plenty of property. The exemption applies only in the narrow case where the estate was exactly five סלעים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather' – drops the earlier answer for a new one
'Really, actually' – goes back to a case set aside earlier
'What case are we dealing with here?' – narrows the case
סלע coins; five are needed to redeem a firstborn

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Actually, it is where he died after thirty days,
and if there is a lot of property –
indeed, the priest takes it,
and what are we dealing with here?
Where there are only five sela coins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם שֶׁמֵּת לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that רבא just knocked down.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case was that the father died within thirty days, so no lien existed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father died after thirty days, and the estate was only five סלעים. A large estate would be collected from.

steps.title: Background rules: רב אסי's half heirs, half buyers, and a Torah loan
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains his answer with two shared assumptions. First, רב אסי's rule that brothers who divide are half heirs and half buyers. Second, a rule about a loan written in the Torah (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: And everyone accepts רב אסי's view. רב אסי said: Brothers who divided an inheritance are half heirs and half buyers. And everyone agrees that a loan written in the Torah…
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now lays out the rules behind his answer, so we can see why five סלעים leaves the כהן with nothing. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After dividing, each brother holds half his portion as an heir and half as if he bought it from his brother. A debt that is only a Torah obligation, like פדיון הבן, is not treated like a loan written in a document, so it cannot be collected from property that has passed to buyers. רבא will combine these two rules in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan written in the Torah – a money duty from Torah law, not a written loan document

steps.confusionAlert: 'Written in the Torah' does not mean a loan with a written document. It means a money duty that comes from Torah law itself, like פדיון הבן.

phrases.aramaic: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב אַסִּי,
phrases.english: And everyone holds the view of Rav Asi,
as Rav Asi said:
Brothers who divided –
are half heirs and half buyers,
and everyone agrees that a loan written in the Torah
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the rules that will explain רבא's five-סלעים case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Laying out the rules behind the new explanation
steps.terutzMaskana: Two shared rules will explain why, with only five סלעים, the כהן can reach only the half the brothers hold as heirs, two and a half סלעים, which is not a full redemption payment.
